title: Harvard Physical Sciences 2 randomized trial: LLM-based AI tutor (GPT-4) doubles learning gains versus in-class active learning
summary: Harvard PS2 RCT (fall 2023, 194 students): LLM-based tutor (GPT-4) produced over double the learning gains of active-learning class in less time.
account: In autumn 2023, in Harvard University's Physical Sciences 2 course, the course team ran a randomized controlled crossover experiment with 194 students across two topics, surface tension and fluid flow. Each student learned one topic in an in-class active-learning session and the other at home with a purpose-built AI tutor. The paper does not state outright which model the tutor ran on: its Methods say 'we avoided relying solely on GPT-4 to generate solutions for these activities', and its Discussion lists 'a large language model capable of closely following complex prompts (e.g., GPT-4)' among the factors behind the gains. The paper, published in Scientific Reports on 3 June 2025, reports that 'students learn significantly more in less time when using the AI tutor', with median learning gains over double those of the class session, a median of 49 minutes on task, and higher engagement and motivation. The paper places the study in 'the Fall 2023 semester' and 'the ninth and tenth weeks of the course' without a calendar date, so 1 September 2023 is used as a placeholder; the lessons themselves came later in the term.
purpose: The tutor was built to teach these physics lessons with research-based pedagogy; the learning gain was that purpose.
system: Custom AI tutor for Harvard PS2 built on a large language model with research-based pedagogical prompts
developer: Harvard University (Kestin, Miller, Klales, Milbourne, Ponti)
taxonomy_note: Reclassified to the evidence base: the outcome is a class-level aggregate from an RCT, not an individually attributable event.

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: a randomized trial reporting class-level learning gains; cohort-level evidence is not placed on the scale. Students in the AI condition scored higher on a post-test for one lesson (median gains over double) in a median of 49 minutes; a small, short-term benefit per student.

General benefit without an event: a randomized trial reporting class-level learning gains; cohort-level evidence is not placed on the scale. The course gained evidence for a lesson format that teaches a topic in less time with higher reported engagement.

ai_role.statement: The LLM delivered the instruction; the comparison condition was active learning taught in class. The authors credit the research-based design (prompts, scaffolding) alongside the model.

evidence.citation: Kestin G, Miller K, Klales A, Milbourne T, Ponti G (2025). AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting. Scientific Reports (PMC12179260).
evidence.title: AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting
evidence.quote: students learn significantly more in less time when using the AI tutor, compared with the in-class active learning

produced_by: Lesson content pre-structured by instructors into the tutor
Prompts enforcing research-based pedagogy rather than answer-giving
Students with access to the tutor at home and a pre/post test design
must_hold: The model follows complex pedagogical prompts
Topics are self-contained and short (two lessons tested)

echoes.setting: Edo State, Nigeria: six-week after-school program (June-July 2024; first day of month used) for first-year senior secondary students in Benin City using Microsoft Copilot (GPT-4); 0.31 SD overall, 0.23 SD in English; World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125 (May 2025)
echoes.source: ERIC record ED676624 https://eric.ed.gov/?q=source:%22World+Bank%22&id=ED676624 (quote: 'a significant improvement of 0.31 standard deviation'); World Bank blog 9 Jan 2025 https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/education/From-chalkboards-to-chatbots-Transforming-learning-in-Nigeria (quote: 'equivalent to nearly two years of typical learning in just six weeks')

paired_incident.title: AllHere's Chatbot 'Ed' Fails and Costs Los Angeles Unified School District $6 Million
paired_incident.basis: Student-facing AI learning assistant: Harvard's GPT-4 tutor doubled learning gains, while LAUSD's AllHere chatbot 'Ed' failed to deliver academic support, costing the district up to $6 million and leaving students without it.

headline: Harvard's GPT-4 tutor more than doubles median learning gains
metric: median learning gains over double those of the class session

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.
Paired with AI Incident Database incident 793 (medium confidence); severity not given by the source.

Softened the title and summary from 'GPT-4-based' to 'LLM-based (GPT-4)' and quoted the Methods and Discussion sentences in the account as the paper's only basis for naming GPT-4, corrected the date disclosure to say that the paper places the lessons in the ninth and tenth weeks of the Fall 2023 semester with 1 September used as a placeholder, and dropped 'public' from the Nigeria echo setting because neither cited source states it.
